title: Retries and Failure Policies knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Retries and Failure Policies”?
options: Status returned by the last command
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Bounded retry attempts” under lesson 127, “Retries and Failure Policies”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Retries and Failure Policies”?
options: Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
questions.answer_key: Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics.
questions.explanation: Use syntax checks, explicit error handling, and actionable diagnostics. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Retries and Failure Policies”?
options: Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output.
questions.answer_key: Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output.
questions.explanation: Check the relevant command statuses immediately and report failures instead of inferring success from output. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
